incident: Diavol ransomware (BazarLoader ISO/LNK to domain-wide Diavol)

sources.title: Diavol Ransomware - The DFIR Report (2021-12-13)
sources.what_it_gave: entry (phishing OneDrive -> zip/ISO/LNK -> BazarLoader via rundll32), hops (beachhead->file server via RDP/CS reverse proxy, AnyDesk RDP to other servers, pivot to DC and backup server), cred access (reg hives, Kerberoast/AS-REP Rubeus, LSASS on DC via Task Manager, Veeam creds via DPAPI), exfil (FileZilla SFTP ~200MB), impact (Diavol via RDP + kill.bat), ~32-42h

narrative_before: In this 2021 intrusion the DFIR Report observed a phishing email with a OneDrive link delivering a zip containing an ISO (Documents.lnk + DLL); the LNK ran BazarLoader via rundll32 on a beachhead endpoint (C2 to 159.223.31.75 / 206.189.49.239). After ~1h of inactivity Cobalt Strike DLL beacons dropped; AdFind ran twice, registry hives (SAM/SECURITY/SYSTEM) were dumped via fodhelper_reg_hashes.bat, and a BITS job re-ran the ISO every ~3h. After ~18h, network scanning (Advanced IP Scanner, MSSQLUDPScanner) and Rubeus Kerberoast/AS-REP ran. The first hop was RDP (through the Cobalt Strike reverse proxy) to a file server, where AnyDesk and FileZilla were installed; AnyDesk RDP reached other servers. The actors pivoted to a domain controller (LSASS dumped via Task Manager, uploaded to ufile.io) and a Veeam backup server (Veeam creds dumped via sqlcmd and decrypted via DPAPI, all over RDP). FileZilla exfiltrated ~200MB over SFTP to 192.52.167[.]210. On day 3 a ping sweep from the file server preceded RDP to all machines and kill.bat (shadow-copy deletion, service stops) before Diavol encrypted domain-wide; time to ransom was ~32-42h.

detection_moments.description: BazarLoader + Cobalt Strike on the beachhead; registry hives dumped; after ~18h Rubeus Kerberoast/AS-REP and network scanning.
detection_moments.evidence: 'Registry hive dumps (SAM, SECURITY, SYSTEM) via fodhelper_reg_hashes.bat ... Kerberoasting and AS-REP roasting: Rubeus, after the roughly 18-hour gap' - Diavol Ransomware, The DFIR Report

detection_moments.description: First hop RDP to the file server (AnyDesk/FileZilla); pivot to a DC (LSASS via Task Manager) and Veeam backup server (creds via DPAPI); FileZilla exfil ~200MB.
detection_moments.evidence: 'one of the domain controllers had LSASS dumped using Task Manager ... Veeam credentials dumped via sqlcmd ... decryption performed with a DPAPI-based C# program ... FileZilla over SFTP ... about 200MB' - Diavol Ransomware

detection_moments.description: Day 3: ping sweep from the file server, RDP to all machines, kill.bat (vssadmin shadow delete, service stops) then Diavol encrypts domain-wide.
detection_moments.evidence: 'a ping sweep from a compromised file server, then RDP to all machines ... kill.bat ... Deleted volume shadow copies ... The ransomware was run manually over RDP on each machine' - Diavol Ransomware

attack_path: phishing OneDrive zip/ISO/LNK runs BazarLoader via rundll32 (T1566.002/T1204.002)
RDP (through Cobalt Strike reverse proxy) to a file server; AnyDesk + FileZilla installed (T1021.001)
pivot to a domain controller via RDP/AnyDesk; LSASS dumped via Task Manager (T1021.001/T1003.001)
RDP to Veeam backup server; Veeam creds dumped via sqlcmd and decrypted via DPAPI (T1021.001/T1003)
ping sweep then RDP to all machines; kill.bat and Diavol run manually (T1021.001/T1486/T1490)
ambiguities: Hosts named by role only; victim sector not stated. 'Multiple clients'/'all machines' modelled as pc_2/pc_3.
Time to ransom is reported inconsistently (~32h intro vs ~42h body); logged as ~32-42h.
Domain admin acquisition not explicitly confirmed; lateral RDP 'most likely' used dumped creds.
Moments are the report's own timeline markers (beachhead/cred access, RDP pivots, encryption), not a defender detection timeline.
